endorsements.title: Guardrails for GenAI drafted replies in patient portal messaging
endorsements.issuer: Sakr J. npj Digital Medicine 2026;9 (PMID 41942581, doi:10.1038/s41746-026-02621-6)
endorsements.quote: - Tier 3 (high risk): drafting disabled or mandatory second check (team member or structured checklist) + documentation of reasoning.

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether disabling one-click sending or AI drafting for high-risk patient messages reduces erroneous replies, and no supplied study documents how often such errors occur. The recommendation rests on a single commentary that treats disabling drafting as one of two acceptable options for high-risk messages.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies of the practice and zero studies of the hazard. The only support is one commentary rated as a must, which is expert opinion. Under GRADE conventions, this yields no direct evidence, and the size and direction of any effect on reply errors or patient outcomes remain unknown.

The endorsing commentary allows either disabled drafting or a mandatory second check with documented reasoning for high-risk messages. These two safeguards act at different points. One removes the AI draft, and the other adds a human check before sending. No supplied data show which, if either, catches errors before they reach patients.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare high-risk message tiers with AI drafting disabled, with one-click sending removed, and with a mandatory second check. These studies should measure how often erroneous replies reach patients, time to clinician response for urgent messages, and how accurately messages are assigned to the high-risk tier.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. It is unknown whether tiering rules classify messages from these patients accurately or whether restrictions change response times for them.
